questions.question: In AWS Network Core terms, what does the Systems Development Manager primarily lead?
options: System Development Engineers building software that builds/operates/monitors/assures regional network fabrics
Only customer VPC Solutions Architects
Only physical cable plant technicians with no software
Only marketing for Direct Connect
questions.explanation: JD: SDM over SysDEs bridging DC ops capabilities with software solutions.

questions.question: Network Development Engineers (NDEs) on Clos/fabric teams typically own:
options: Fabric design, routing/availability/compliance, and safe network change at DC scale
Only React front-ends
Only payroll systems
Only S3 object APIs
questions.explanation: Sibling NDE Clos/ARC JDs: availability, routing, compliance of Clos DC networks.

questions.question: SysDEs on Core Network / Network Core software planes are closest to:
options: SRE-like engineers whose customers are network engineers and the fabric tooling itself
Retail store associates
External enterprise account managers only
GPU model trainers only
questions.explanation: Public SysDE Core Network JDs: tools/services that build, operate, monitor, assure the AWS network.

questions.question: A Clos / spine-leaf fabric is preferred in large DCs mainly because it:
options: Provides scalable, predictable east-west bandwidth with ECMP and limited blast radius per failure
Eliminates the need for any routing protocol
Guarantees zero packet loss forever without ops
Only works for Wi-Fi campuses
questions.explanation: InterviewStack / Clos design: non-blocking scale-out fabric pattern.

questions.question: Using eBGP as a Clos underlay (RFC 7938-style) primarily buys:
options: Simple horizontal scale and ECMP with well-understood failure domains vs complex IGP flooding
Automatic TLS termination
Free CDN capacity
Removal of all monitoring needs
questions.explanation: RFC 7938 / Clos BGP underlay pattern common in hyperscale DC fabrics.

questions.question: The primary internal customers of Network Core software are:
options: NDEs and DC/network ops who need reliable automation, visibility, and safe change tooling
Only end-consumers shopping on amazon.com
Only third-party phone OEMs
Only external ISP NOCs
questions.explanation: SysDE Core Network framing: internal network engineering customers.

questions.question: Availability, Routing, and Compliance (ARC) style fabric work focuses on:
options: Keeping Clos networks security-compliant while planned/unplanned events don’t hurt customer performance
Writing mobile ads
Designing Kindle UI themes
Managing retail inventory only

questions.question: DC Life Cycle (refresh/turndown) network work succeeds when:
options: Processes run safely with no impact to customer traffic and automation reduces manual risk
Devices are yanked without coordination
Only Excel trackers matter, not validation
Customer impact is accepted as inevitable
questions.explanation: DCLC NDE JD: operational excellence during refresh/exit.

questions.question: As SDM Network Core, Dive Deep during a fabric tool outage means:
options: Reading metrics/logs/config diffs with engineers and driving mitigation + durable fix—not only status meetings
Delegating forever without understanding mechanisms
Waiting for customers to file public tweets
Rewriting the LP wiki
questions.explanation: JD: dive into details, make technical contributions, drive reliability.

questions.question: Network Core is NOT primarily about:
options: Day-to-day customer VPC architecture consulting as a Solutions Architect
Software platforms for regional fabric build/ops/monitor/assure
Partnering with NDEs on operability
Raising standards for change safety tooling
questions.explanation: Role boundary: foundation fabric software plane vs customer SA work.

questions.question: In a Clos with ECMP, losing one spine typically should:
options: Reduce capacity but keep connectivity if remaining paths and hashing still serve flows
Black-hole the entire region permanently by design
Require manual IP renumbering of every host
Disable BGP worldwide
questions.explanation: ECMP resilience is a core fabric interview signal.

questions.question: Utility Computing (UC) context for this role means Network Core supports:
options: Foundational AWS infrastructure that compute/storage/database services depend on
Only Alexa skill marketing
Only Twitch esports brackets
Only Whole Foods POS themes
questions.explanation: JD places the team in UC supporting foundational services.

questions.question: A healthy Network Core SDM roadmap balances:
options: NDE/ops customer asks, platform reliability debt, and scalable automation investments with clear priority
Only vanity features with no operability
Never saying no to any request
Ignoring incidents to ship slides
questions.explanation: JD: roadmaps + operating existing systems at high quality.

questions.question: For the AU Systems Development Manager Network Core posting, AGSVA awareness means:
options: You must be eligible/able to attain clearance; treat it as a hard process gate, not a trivia quiz
Clearance replaces all technical interviews
Foreign classified details should be discussed in STAR stories
AGSVA is optional branding only
questions.explanation: JD + AGSVA eligibility; keep stories unclassified.

questions.question: When prioritizing a fabric automation bug, the SDM should weigh first:
options: Customer-visible blast radius and correlated failure risk across the fabric
Only whether the ticket is old
Only the author’s job level
Whether the bug title uses emoji
questions.explanation: Customer Obsession + Highest Standards on blast radius.

questions.question: Driving organizational standards for resiliency as Network Core SDM looks like:
options: Mechanisms: review bars, canary/rollback defaults, SLOs, and shared runbooks—not heroics
Asking people to try harder without tools
Banning all changes forever
Outsourcing ownership of every Sev
questions.explanation: JD: standards for operational excellence and resiliency.
